newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury's 10-yr note yield seen at 6.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury's 10-yr note yield seen at 6.50 pct.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury's auction of $10 billion in 10-year notes on Tuesday is expected to produce a yield near 6.50 percent, dealers said.
Analysts said there was rumored interest from Japanese investors. Portfolios of mortgage-backed securities are also potential buyers, they said.
At 1251 EDT/1651 GMT, the 10-year notes were quoted at 6.50 percent in when-issued trade.
The bidding deadline for the notes is 1300 EDT/1700 GMT and results are expected around 1345 EDT/1745 GMT.

"Where the 10-years are trading at one o'clock is where it's going to come," said Patrick Dimick, Treasury market analyst at CS First Boston. "That's really what defines the success of an auction, whether it stops out where it was at one o'clock." -- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1679
